sources.note: Livy 3.26, Rev. Canon Roberts translation (via WebFetch extraction).

facts.claim: Cincinnatus served as dictator in 458 or 457 BC to defend against the Aequi; the army under L. Minucius Esquilinus Augurinus was besieged.
facts.verbatim_support: Cincinnatus served as dictator...in 458 or 457 BC; the Aequi quickly deployed around their position and successfully besieged them.

facts.claim: The senate's deputation found him digging a ditch or ploughing.
facts.verbatim_support: There he was found by the deputation from the senate either digging out a ditch or ploughing

facts.claim: He cultivated a four-acre field on the other side of the Tiber.
facts.verbatim_support: L. Quinctius, used to cultivate a four-acre field on the other side of the Tiber

facts.claim: The deputation saluted him as Dictator.
facts.verbatim_support: the deputation saluted him as Dictator and congratulated him

facts.claim: The Aequi, attacked on both sides, turned to supplication and were sent under a yoke of three spears.
facts.verbatim_support: they turned from fighting to supplication...This was made of three spears...Under this yoke the Dictator sent the Aequi.

facts.claim: Quinctius resigned on the sixteenth day the dictatorship conferred on him for six months.
facts.verbatim_support: Quinctius resigned on the sixteenth day the dictatorship which had been conferred upon him for six months.
facts.verification_note: Wikipedia says 'fifteen days' in one sentence and 'sixteen days' in another; the video follows Livy.

numbers.label: Term of office
numbers.verbatim_support: conferred upon him for six months
